title: Build Your First Nodics Capability
readerIntent: Understand the safe end-to-end path for adding one project-owned business capability.
priorKnowledge: Complete the local setup and understand basic APIs and data models.
summary: Start with ownership and contracts, reuse existing capabilities, add only necessary layers, and prove positive and rejected behavior.

sections.heading: Example outcome
paragraphs: Imagine a project needs tenant-owned service requests that authorized employees can create, view, update, and close. Treat that outcome as one project capability rather than scattering it across framework modules.

sections.heading: Implementation sequence
items: Search for an existing authority and extension point.
Choose the project module that owns the capability.
Describe data, permissions, tenant ownership, states, integrations, failures, and customization.
Add schema, service, API, configuration, event, or pipeline layers only when each has a responsibility.
Regenerate derived artifacts from source definitions.
Update canonical documentation and the concise module README.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Successful create, read, update, and close behavior.
State boundaries such as closing an already closed request.
Contract, integration, generated-artifact, and regression behavior.

sections.heading: What not to do
items: Do not modify reusable framework code for a customer-only rule.
Do not create a second loader, registry, workflow, or persistence authority.
Do not edit generated artifacts as the long-term source.
Do not declare completion while tests or documentation are stale.
